justification: Gap: “the pitch does a ___ trade from eleven until the light goes” following “three hundred and forty of them go out on the east beach at a pound and ten pence a day”. “Does a brisk trade” is the fixed collocation for lively, high-volume business, which is exactly what the all-day count of hires describes. A hasty killed: connotes rushed and careless action, not volume of business; nothing in the sentence wants carelessness. B rapid and C swift killed: both describe speed of motion or of a single process and do not collocate with “trade” in the sense of business done — “a rapid/swift trade” would suggest one quick exchange, not a day-long run of hires.

Gap: “three hundred and thirty-six chairs that had ___ there since breakfast” — past perfect of the intransitive verb lie (be in a resting position) is “had lain”; the chairs are the resting subject. A lie killed: bare infinitive after “had”, ungrammatical. C laid killed: past participle of transitive lay, which requires an object (“had laid the chairs”); here nothing is being placed, the chairs themselves rest. D lay killed: lay is the simple past of lie, not a participle, so “had lay” is ungrammatical.

The paragraph before the gap frames a contrast: “What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing.” Sentence one states the nominal side — “The hire is the whole of the transaction, and it has risen by ten pence in a decade”; the gap sentence states the de facto side — “the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile between the pier and the sailing club, and Carol Gregson the one person on it who is stationary and paid” — so the connective must mark the turn from formal transaction to actual function: “In practice”. A In principle killed: reverses the logic — the hire is what holds in principle; the staffed-thing role is what holds in fact. B In addition killed: treats the two sentences as a list of like facts and loses the charges-for/does opposition the paragraph is built on. D In short killed: signals a summary, but the gap sentence introduces new material (the mile, Gregson, nine seasons) rather than compressing sentence one.

Gap: “Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she ___ that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint.” Under pressure she grants the point in part (yes, in August they interrupt) — “concedes”. C volunteers killed: to volunteer is to offer unprompted, directly contradicted by “Pressed on”. B boasts killed: nothing in the content is a boast; the tail calls it “a description”. D confesses killed: colours the reply as an admission of something personal or discreditable, which “a description rather than a complaint” expressly denies; concedes carries the pressed-into-granting sense without the guilt. Weighed A vs D seriously: both are compatible with “Pressed”, but the appositive tail rules out the confessional register and leaves concedes alone.

Gap: “It was well signed and it was free, but it was ___ used, and it shut after its second summer.” The concessive “but” and the closure demand a word meaning hardly at all: “barely used”. A widely killed: contradicts “but” and the shutting. C strongly killed: not a frequency collocate of “used”, and would likewise contradict the closure. B scantily killed: collocates with clad, dressed, furnished — not with “used”; unidiomatic even though its sense (sparsely) points the right way, and the passage’s own register elsewhere is plain idiom.

Carrying span: “Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin. The hole you measured with your hand is a slot by then. A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through” — which explains why going “up two mesh sizes” failed: “They did not. A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before.” A killed: judged over “A whole spring”, not a single trip. B killed: “The plaice were much as before, a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape” — no change for plaice is reported, and the option’s reasoning inverts the text (flat fish match the stretched slot; nothing is said about squares being the wrong shape for them). C killed: “The second change was to the hanging, not the size” — the hanging came second; the first change was mesh size.

Carrying span: “The second entries were not continuations: each named a different trade, each ran its seven years from the day of sealing, and each fell three to six years after the first.” A fresh seven-year term sealed three to six years into a seven-year first term runs three to six years past the day the first would have ended, so the boys were bound for years beyond that day. B killed: “Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards” — the masters did not give up their trades. C killed: “Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced” — only two families were in the town. D killed: “In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum”, and Ward himself went from “eleven pounds” to “fourteen pounds”.

Bärande span: “Bidraget till enskilda vägar var två kronor per meter och år … oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen. Kvillnäsvägen är 5,4 kilometer lång … Ulvbråtsvägen … är 1,8 kilometer” → 5 400 × 2 = 10 800 kr mot 1 800 × 2 = 3 600 kr, exakt tre gånger (“Räkna gärna själv”). A fälls: “oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen”. B fälls: per hushåll fick Kvillnäs 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr och Ulvbråt 3 600/24 = 150 kr — omvänt förhållande, vilket är författarens egen poäng: “Ett bidrag som mäts i meter och inte i hushåll gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest”. D fälls: “Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören”.

Bärande span: “Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak”, “Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen”, “Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka” samt kravet “Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten”. A fälls: “svek mot landsbygden” är Sarvheds linje, om vilken författaren säger “jag tycker inte att den är riktig”. C fälls: “jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll”. D fälls: han argumenterar mot en ny vändplan vid bron (180 000 kr, “drygt tio vintrars plogning”, marken inte inlöst) och vill att plogbilen fortsätter till den befintliga vändplanen vid Kvillnäs; han begär inget uppskov i väntan på bygge.

Gap: "the pitch does a ___ trade from eleven until the light goes". "does a brisk trade" is the fixed collocation for busy commerce, and the context is volume (three hundred and forty chairs out at a pound and ten pence a day). A hasty killed: hasty means hurried and careless, describes an action's manner, and does not collocate with "trade" as business volume. B rapid and C swift killed: both describe speed of motion or change ("a rapid rise", "a swift reply"); "a rapid/swift trade" is not idiomatic for a stall doing good business. D is the only option that yields the standard phrase.

Gap: "three hundred and thirty-six chairs that had ___ there since breakfast". After "had" the slot needs a past participle of the intransitive verb lie (to be in a resting position): "had lain". A lie killed: base form cannot follow "had". D lay killed: simple past of lie ("the chairs lay there"), not a participle. C laid killed: participle of the transitive verb lay (to put something down), which needs an object ("had laid the chairs"); the chairs here are the subject resting on the racks, so "laid" is ungrammatical.

Gap: "The hire is the whole of the transaction, and it has risen by ten pence in a decade. ___, the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile between the pier and the sailing club". The preceding paragraph frames the contrast — "What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing" — so the sentence pairs the nominal transaction (the hire) against the actual function (the one staffed, stationary person), which is "In practice". A In principle killed: it inverts the contrast; being the one staffed thing is the concrete fact, not the theory. B In addition killed: the relation is opposition, not accumulation; the paragraph is built on the charged-for/done mismatch. D In short killed: it would introduce a summary, but the sentence introduces new information (the mile, the sailing club, Carol Gregson).

Gap: "Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she ___ that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint". "Pressed" signals an admission drawn out under questioning, and admitting they are "an interruption" grants the questioner a point — that is "concedes". C volunteers killed by "Pressed": volunteering is unprompted, the opposite of being pressed. B boasts killed: calling questions an interruption is no boast, and the coda calls it a description. D confesses killed: it imports guilt or wrongdoing, which the coda "a description rather than a complaint" explicitly disclaims; she is granting a fact, not owning up to a fault.

Gap: "It was well signed and it was free, but it was ___ used, and it shut after its second summer". The "but" and the closure require low use: "barely used". A widely and C strongly killed: both assert heavy use, contradicting "but" and "it shut". B scantily killed: "scantily" collocates with clothing or furnishing ("scantily clad"), not with "used"; the natural adverb of degree for use is "barely" (or hardly/little). D is the only grammatical and idiomatic fit.

Carrying span: "Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin. The hole you measured with your hand is a slot by then. A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through" — towing narrows the mesh to a slot, so the two extra sizes did not give a round fish its width, which is why "They did not" see themselves out. A killed: he judged over a season, "A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before", not a single trip. B killed: "The plaice were much as before, a flat fish and a stretched mesh being much the same shape" — the plaice were unchanged by the turned meshes, not newly retained. C killed: "The second change was to the hanging, not the size" — the hanging was the second change; going up two mesh sizes was the first.

Carrying spans: "none for any term but seven years" and "each ran its seven years from the day of sealing, and each fell three to six years after the first" — a second seven-year term sealed three to six years into a seven-year first term ends ten to thirteen years after the first sealing, i.e. years beyond the day the first term would have ended (Ward: 1751 to 1758 versus 1755 to 1762). B killed: "Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards" — the masters did not give up their trades. C killed: "Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced". D killed: "In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum", and Ward's own went from eleven to fourteen pounds.

Bärande span: "två kronor per meter och år, och det betalades ut till samfälligheten oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen"; Kvillnäsvägen 5,4 km mot Ulvbråtsvägen 1,8 km ger 10 800 kr mot 3 600 kr, exakt tre gånger så mycket ("Räkna gärna själv"). A dödas: "oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen". B dödas: per hushåll får Kvillnäs 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr och Ulvbråt 3 600/24 = 150 kr — texten säger det själv: "gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest". D dödas: "Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören".

Bärande span: "Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak", "Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen", "Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka" och sedan "Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten". A dödas: "svek mot landsbygden" är Gudrun Sarvheds linje, och författaren säger "jag tycker inte att den är riktig". C dödas: "jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll". D dödas: han argumenterar mot vändplanen ("kostar alltså drygt tio vintrars plogning") och vill ha fortsatt plogning i driftbudgeten, inte ett uppskov tills en vändplan byggts.

Four near-synonyms for fast with no gap text. 'hasty' carries the only negative connotation, an odd-one-out shape, but that points in no reliable direction. Pure chance; 'rapid' picked as the most collocationally neutral.

lie/lay/laid/lain grammar gap with no sentence. Each form is correct in some frame; nothing in the option set favours one. Chance; 'lay' picked because it covers two frames (past of lie, base of lay).

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: 'In principle' and 'In practice' are contradictories on one variable (theory vs practice), advertising that the gap contrasts one with the other; 'In addition' and 'In short' are unpaired fillers, so the pair alone narrows to two (50 percent)
justification: I cannot see which side of the contrast the gap sits on; I picked 'In practice' because it is the more common pivot after a stated principle. Student-available form channel; halves the field but does not decide it.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (sub-threshold): 'concedes' and 'confesses' are near-synonyms (both admit something unwelcome) and 'boasts' is the sole positive-valence verb; a near-synonym-elimination heuristic would push toward 'boasts'/'volunteers', but the two admitting verbs are distinguishable in context so the heuristic is unreliable
justification: Reporting-verb gap with no sentence; valence and speaker unknown. 'concedes' picked as the commonest argumentative-prose choice. Not above chance.
Degree adverbs with no sentence: two quantity-negative ('scantily', 'barely'), two intensifiers ('widely', 'strongly'). 'scantily' is the rare odd-one-out but that shape is not directional. Chance.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form): B and D are the two options that carry an explanatory clause (B: 'a flat fish being the wrong shape for a square'; D: 'so the extra size did not give a round fish its width') and B is the longest option; A and C are bare procedural claims

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (domain): both B and D state real fisheries facts (square mesh retains flatfish that escape open diamond mesh; diamond mesh narrows under tow so nominal size overstates the opening), which confirms the B/D pair as the plausible set but cannot choose between them
justification: Form and domain knowledge together narrow to B or D, roughly even; I picked D as the premise-type statement ('what is said about the cod end'). Calibration: the form channel is student-available; the mesh-geometry knowledge is not something a Swedish 18-year-old would have.

findings: ENTAILMENT (stem-to-option, near): 'bound twice' all but presupposes a second indenture running past the point the first would have ended, so A is derivable from the stem without the passage unless the second binding was only for the remainder of the first term
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form): A is the only inference-shaped option, matching 'what is suggested'; B and D open with 'The five', universal claims about all five boys that read as over-generalisations
justification: A at about 50 percent. It fails only if the boys were turned over to finish their original terms, which the wording 'bound twice' (rather than 'turned over') argues against. B, C and D each need a specific textual fact I cannot see. Student-available logic channel; borderline kill.

A, B and C are drawn from one small world (two roads, per-household amounts, a ratio) and D from another (contractor fee per trip). A and B are only softly opposed (proportional to residents vs more per household could both hold with different household sizes), so no clean pair; C and D are number claims I cannot check. A picked as the principle statement; chance.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form): B is the balanced 'beslutet är riktigt, men ...' concession with a concrete partial remedy, the shape HP LÄS author-stance keys usually take; A is emotive ('svek'), C absolutising ('hela bygden'), D conditional

PAIR_STRUCTURE (presupposition): B presupposes an existing turnaround ('vändplanen') that is being ploughed to, D presupposes none exists yet at the bridge ('tills en vändplan har anlagts'); they cannot both be true, advertising that the turnaround's existence is settled by the text
justification: B at about 50 percent on form; A is the live alternative if the writer is polemical. Student-available.

findings: ONE-WAY LEAK: none. q2's options carry clauses ('även om kommunen behöver spara', 'plogningen till vändplanen bör fortsätta', 'eftersom vägen behövs för hela bygden', 'tills en vändplan har anlagts vid bron') that assert facts about savings, ploughing, the turnaround and the bridge, none of which is what q1 tests (the basis or size of the old subsidy); q1's options assert nothing about the decision or the writer's stance that q2 tests

SYMMETRIC VOUCHING: weak, single link. q1-D ('entreprenören 400 kronor per tur') and q2-B ('plogningen ... bör fortsätta') share the plough-contractor sub-world; believing one makes the other's world more plausible but not its truth. The remaining q1 world (two roads, per-household ratio) and q2 world (decision, turnaround, bridge) are disjoint
justification: Joint stems-only solvability is low: q1 at chance (pick A), q2 around 50 percent on form (pick B), and the two are effectively independent; answering either does not shift the odds on the other beyond the marginal D-B plausibility link.

A ‘hasty’ dies collocationally — hasty describes a rushed or careless single act, never sustained commerce; ‘does a hasty trade’ is not English. B ‘rapid’ dies collocationally — ‘does a rapid trade’ is not idiomatic; rapid names the speed of a process, not the liveliness of business. C ‘swift’ is the nearest live alternative but dies on the same ground plus context: swift is the speed of a quick single action, while the gap spans hours (‘from eleven until the light goes’) and needs liveliness of business — ‘does a brisk trade’ (key D) is the fixed collocation.

A ‘lie’ dies grammatically — ‘had lie’ is not a form. C ‘laid’ dies — past participle of transitive ‘lay’, which needs an object; the chairs ‘had lain there’ is intransitive, so ‘had laid there’ is the classic error, not a second answer in a text of this register. D ‘lay’ dies — simple past, not a participle; ‘had lay’ is ungrammatical. Key B ‘lain’ is the only past participle of intransitive ‘lie’ that fits ‘had ___ there since breakfast’.

A ‘In principle’ dies on direction: the sentence after the gap states the pitch’s actual de-facto role (‘the one staffed thing on the mile … the one person on it who is stationary and paid’), the reality side of the contrast announced by ‘What the pitch charges for and what it does are not the same thing’; the formal side is already given by ‘The hire is the whole of the transaction’. B ‘In addition’ is the nearest survivor but dies on that same structural cue: the paragraph is explicitly built as charges-for versus does, and ‘the whole of the transaction’ is a restrictive claim the next sentence must qualify, not extend — an additive marker breaks the announced contrast. D ‘In short’ dies — the sentence after the gap does not summarize the sentence before it (a ten-pence rise in a decade); it introduces new content. Key C ‘In practice’.

findings: D: ‘confesses’ is a live near-synonym of the key — ‘Pressed on whether she minds the questions, she confesses that in August they are an interruption …’ is grammatical, idiomatic and register-appropriate; it is killed by nuance (confess = own up to something personal or discreditable; concede = grant a point under pressure) and by the coda ‘a description rather than a complaint’, not by a hard textual span.
justification: B ‘boasts’ dies — the content is not self-praise and the coda calls it description. C ‘volunteers’ dies on ‘Pressed on’ — a volunteered remark is unprompted; this one was extracted under pressure. D ‘confesses’: best case — British ‘I confess’ is frequently light; she is pressed and admits that the questions are an interruption in August, and the author then softens it as description; nothing in the sentence is ungrammatical or unidiomatic with ‘confesses’. Against D — ‘confess’ frames the object as a personal admission of minding, which is exactly what ‘a description rather than a complaint’ denies, and the second half of the object (‘by late September most of the job’) is not confession-shaped; ‘concede’ pairs with ‘Pressed on’ as the standard journalistic collocation (pressed → conceded) and fits the grant-then-reframe structure. Key A is the best answer, but D is survivable with effort and its kill is a subtle reading; flag, not kill.

A ‘widely’ dies on ‘but’ and ‘it shut after its second summer’ — the clause must explain failure despite being well signed and free. B ‘scantily’ has the right direction but dies collocationally — ‘scantily’ collocates with clad/dressed/furnished, not with ‘used’; the word for this slot would be ‘sparsely’ or ‘little’, and neither is offered. C ‘strongly’ dies on both direction and collocation (‘strongly used’ is not English). Key D ‘barely used’.

Mechanism check: physically correct — diamond meshes under tow tension elongate along the tow axis and close laterally (‘every mesh pulls long and thin’, ‘a slot by then’), so a round-bodied haddock cannot get its width through, and hanging the same twine on the bar (‘turned right round the bag’) gives square meshes that stay open under drag; the key is not backwards. A dies on ‘A whole spring on, the boxes at the harbour looked much as they had the year before’ — a season, not a single trip. B dies on ‘The plaice were much as before’ — the text asserts no change, B asserts one (in the world square mesh does tend to cut flatfish escape, so B is world-plausible but text-contradicted; fair). C dies on ‘The second change was to the hanging, not the size’ — size came first. Key D matches ‘Tow it, and every mesh pulls long and thin … A haddock is round, and it has to get its width through.’

B dies on ‘Each of the first masters went on enrolling boys of his own for years afterwards’. C dies on ‘Of the five fathers, two lived in the town, one farmed nine miles off, one combed wool in the next county, and one the clerk left unplaced’ — not the five. D dies on ‘In three of the five the second premium was the larger sum’ and on Ward’s own eleven→fourteen pounds. Key A: each second binding ‘ran its seven years from the day of sealing’ and ‘fell three to six years after the first’, so it ends three to six years past the day the first term would have ended.

A dies on ‘oavsett hur många som bodde vid vägen’. B dies on the arithmetic the text invites (‘Räkna gärna själv’): 10 800/4 = 2 700 kr per household at Kvillnäs against 3 600/24 = 150 at Ulvbråt, and on ‘gynnar den som bor glest, och det är vi som bor glest’ — reversed. D dies on ‘Den plogningen har för övrigt aldrig legat i bidraget utan i kommunens avtal med entreprenören’. Key C: 5 400 m × 2 kr = 10 800 vs 1 800 × 2 = 3 600, exactly three times.

A is Sarvhed’s line and dies on ‘Jag tror ändå att den linjen förlorar, och jag tycker inte att den är riktig’. C dies on ‘Bidraget var orättvist, och jag begär det inte tillbaka – inte heller ett nytt räknat per hushåll’. D dies on ‘Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer. Låt plogbilen gå ända fram till vändplanen och lägg sträckan i driftbudgeten’ — he wants ploughing to the existing Kvillnäs vändplan, argues against building one at the bridge (‘drygt tio vintrars plogning’), and never asks for a delay (‘Jag har inget att invända mot besparingen’). Key B: ‘Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak’ plus the 1,9-kilometre demand.

Vote 1: read aloud as a native – title, passage (byte-identical to r1, re-read in full anyway), glossary, both prompts, eight options (both sets rewritten) and both rationales (heavily rewritten). The insändare is unforced Swedish throughout: ”Räkna gärna själv”, ”Kommunen har alltså haft rätt i sak”, ”Ska plogbilen vända där, måste en vändplan anläggas”, ”drygt tio vintrars plogning”, ”Det jag begär är 1,9 kilometer”, ”jag tänker inte påstå att jag vet”. The new options read as a native item-writer would phrase them (”fick mer per hushåll än”, ”gav entreprenören 400 kronor per tur”, ”även om kommunen behöver spara”, ”bör skjutas upp tills en vändplan har anlagts”). Every r1 vote-1 finding is discharged: ”vilket texten skiljer på i klartext” is now ”en skillnad som texten gör i klartext”; ”Per hushåll skiljer det arton gånger” is now ”arton gånger så mycket per hushåll till Kvillnäsvägen, inte mindre”; ”påfallande” is now ”iögonfallande”. Vote 2: systematic form sweep. The passage is a debattinsändare and stays one: concessive opening, a delimited demand, a named opponent, place and signature, the committee date as coda. ”Räkna gärna själv” is reader address of exactly the kind the genre licenses. No drift toward blog, chat or translationese. The rationales are the part the repair rewrote most, so I read them for English metawords and generator-speak: ”KEY C:” / ”KEY B:” are now ”Rätt svar C:” / ”Rätt svar B:”, and the English taxonomy labels (reversed_causality, scope_shift, surface_lexical_echo, attribution_swap, plausible_worldknowledge, detail_as_main) have been replaced by Swedish teacherly parentheses (”den gamla regeln vänd bak och fram”, ”rätt siffror, fel riktning”, ”två avtal som blandas ihop”, ”fel avsändare”, ”en väntad kompromiss som texten avvisar”, ”en detalj upphöjd till huvudsak”) – all idiomatic Swedish and addressed to the student, not to the pipeline. Vote 1, native read-aloud of the gapped passage with the keys inserted, five gap prompts, twenty options and five rationales, with particular weight on the two repaired frames (gap 3 and gap 5) and the extended gap-4 sentence. Nothing a native writer would not produce. The gap-4 frame now reads ‘she concedes that in August they are an interruption and by late September most of the job, a description rather than a complaint’: ‘interruption’ is the right noun (r1’s ‘obstruction’ is gone) and the summative appositive over the reported clause is a normal English move; it is compressed, but the misattachment to ‘most of the job’ fails on sense at once and the intended reading takes over, so it clears. Gap 3 with the key inserted — ‘The hire is the whole of the transaction … In practice, the pitch is the one staffed thing on the mile’ — is idiomatic; ‘In addition’ and ‘In short’ are both live sentence-initial connectives, so the set no longer halves on shape, and neither reads as exotic English. Gap 5: ‘barely used’ is the native fill. ‘scantily used’, judged as asked: NOT a live collocation — ‘scantily’ pairs with clad, dressed, furnished, covered, populated (quantity provided), never with frequency of use; the live minimisers before ‘used’ are little, barely, hardly, scarcely, seldom, rarely, sparsely. A dies on “ett tilloppsdike ut mot myrens övre kant” together with “en vattningsränna går tvärs över sluttningen och faller nästan inte alls” — the ränna sits at the upper edge and runs along the contour, so it cannot be drawn through the middle feeding both sides. B dies on “Avvägningen gjordes med vattenpass och käppar, på de mindre anläggningarna efter ögonmått” — ögonmått is restricted to the smaller works, and Skrömtbäcken’s main ränna is given a measured gradient (“drygt en halv meter på fyrahundra”); the added “sedan vattnet hade släppts på” has no anchor at all. D dies on “Först då lämnade vattnet rännan längs hela dess längd i stället för att följa den till den lägsta punkten och skära sig ner där” — a single outlet is precisely the failure the rule exists to prevent. Key C restates “rännan skulle luta mindre än marken nedanför den” and is confirmed by the two gradients.

Four genuinely distinct, physically real processes, none of them nonsense: sediment/dissolved-nutrient fertilisation (A), oxygen-driven peat mineralisation (B, key), moisture as drought relief (C), and winter-ice frost insulation (D). A is the strongest temptation because it is the standard textbook mechanism of water meadows and the text concedes it operates elsewhere (“Längs de grumligare åarna i söder vägde slammet tyngre än här”) — right in the world, wrong here — but it dies on the sentence pair that names and excludes both of its halves: “Bäckvatten från myrmark är brunt och slamfattigt. Någon nämnvärd mängd mineraljord avlagrades inte på ängarna vid Skrömtbäcken, och halten av löst näring i vattnet var för låg för att ensam förklara skördeökningen.” C dies on “Det avgörande var syret” plus “Stillastående vatten gör tvärtom: det stänger ute luften” — wetness as such is presented as harmful and movement as the whole requirement (“hela den tiden skulle det röra sig”); the water is also “stängdes av ett par veckor före slåttern”, i.e. off before high summer. D is verbatim true as a proposition — P5 says the ice and snow “hindrade tjälen från att gå djupt, så att rötterna klarade sig bättre och tillväxten kom i gång tidigare på våren” — but it is not the huvudorsak the stem asks for: it is scoped to “På en del av markerna”, it belongs to autumn dämning rather than the sixty-day silning that defines the siläng, and the text attaches the stem’s own noun to the oxygen account alone (“för att ensam förklara skördeökningen” → “Det avgörande var syret”). Law 11 is satisfied because the passage designates a single main cause categorically rather than leaving the key merely ‘best’.

All three die on the agreement’s stated content, “fördelade vattnet i turer om fyra dygn och angav i vilken ordning turerna skulle tas”, which is also the key. A additionally lacks any anchor: maintenance appears only as “dämmet skadades av islossningen nästan varje vår”, with no allocation of responsibility. B is wrong on the object (vattnet, not myrhöet) and on the characterisation (a fixed order, not an uneven split). C exploits the adjacent “omkring niohundra dagsverken fördelade på tre somrar”, but the 1858 document allocates water, not digging days. The framing sentence “Till detta kom samordningen” confirms why the author raises it.

B dies on the two stated causal conclusions — “Hennes slutsats är att fodret upphörde att vara knappt” against “Orsaken söker han i arbetskraften, som drogs till sågverken och till Amerika” — so varför is exactly what divides them; timing is the evidence, not the quarrel. C dies on their different corpora: “har jämfört tidpunkterna i ett fyrtiotal socknar” against “har karterat rännsystemen i fyra socknar”, and each objects to the other’s material rather than to a shared reading of one body of evidence. D carries a verbatim-true premise (forty parishes against four) but its causal claim is false: the text roots Nolvide’s objection in selection, not size — “hennes socknar är valda bland dem som har bevarade dikningshandlingar” — and neither scholar raises sample size. Key A is carried by the pair of mutual source objections plus “kartorna sällan går att tidfästa närmare än ett par decennier” and the closing “ingen förde bok över hur många dagar som gick åt till rännorna”.

A dies on “samma jämna blå himmel över taken” — the sky is uniform; the bait, “Himlen ändras på varje kort”, says the sky is altered on every card relative to the plate, not that it differs between cards, and “samma” settles it in the adjacent sentence. C dies on “Nio plåtar har moln, och även på de korten ligger samma jämna blå himmel över taken” — the nine belong to the plåtar and the clouds are painted over on the cards. D dies on “På de flesta plåtarna är den en tom vit yta” plus “plåten kunde inte hålla himlen, alltså fick koloristen ge den en” — white is the plate’s state, and the card is exactly where a sky gets added. Three of the four are plåt/kort inversions, which is the unit’s core skill, and each is killed by an explicit adjacent clause.

A dies on the firm’s own production chain — “Fotograferingen skedde med glasplåt, tryckningen beställdes i Tyskland, och färgen lades på för hand i firmans lokal vid torget”, with “Fyrtioen plåtar finns kvar” — the plates are Vidbring’s own, and buying Vitthamn views from photographers in other towns is nowhere suggested. Noted fairly: A has the right logical shape in the world (bought-in stock images would indeed decouple postmark from exposure), so it is wrong per the text rather than wrong in itself. B dies on “Plåtarna kom till museet 1974, i två packlårar och utan förteckning” and on chronology: the card at issue is postmarked August 1919, inside the firm’s own 1904–1929 run, so no successor after publication ceased could account for it. C is the strongest survivor-candidate — it is true of the world, and “lagret” does appear in the passage — but it still dies on two explicit grounds. First, the stem asks about “när bilden togs”, and shelf time separates a postmark only from the printing, not from the exposure. Second, the passage glosses its own stock category with the reprint mechanism in the very next sentence, “Vidbring tryckte nya upplagor från samma plåt så länge ett motiv gick att sälja”, which is the key; no sentence puts printed cards in shops.

V2 efter framflyttat led: ”till dem hör drygt fyrahundra kort”, ”så återger ortokromatiska emulsioner den”, ”På plåten speglar sig husen”, ”Om andra förlag hade tagit över motiven (B) kunde det ge”. Rationalernas former: ”stycke 4:s uppgift” (kolongenitiv på räkneord, korrekt), ”det enda alternativ som” (obestämt substantiv efter enda + som, standard), ”tio år innan utgivningen upphörde”, ”det enda texten säger om plåtarnas senare öde”. Röst 3: register och genre. Passagen är en kulturhistorisk essä och håller genren ovanligt väl – daterad konkret öppning, räknade belägg, första person som arkivarbetare, inget läsartilltal, ingen bloggton, ingen aforistisk slutkläm; kodan om motiv 44 stänger på en iakttagelse och stannar inne i essäns metod. Vokabulären är äkta arkiv- och fotohistorisk svenska: löneboken, färganvisningar, kolorist, glasplåt, retusch, packlårar, förteckning, motiv, upplaga. Inget engelskt lemma med svensk böjning i något elevsynligt fält (r1:s ”stemmet” och ”hedgeheuristiken” är borta och återkommer inte), inget engelskt metaord, ingen taxonomietikett, ingen laghänvisning. Den här rundans ändringar höjer om något registret: ”säger föga om” är sakprosans egen kvantifierare och inte stelare än genren tål; strykningen av distraktormeningen tar bort det sista item-writer-ordet ur q1-rationalen, som nu slutar på en coachningsmening riktad till eleven; och ”A, B och C skulle alla i sak kunna förklara” ersätter en formulering som talade om hur alternativen var byggda. Det omgjorda q1 A (”Den fick olika färg från kort till kort”) och den nya A-meningen i rationalen ligger i samma neutrala provsvenska som övriga alternativ. Särskilt prövad och friad: q2-rationalens slutmening ”Det rätta svaret är varken det längsta alternativet (A är längre) eller det enda garderade (C har samma ”kunde”), så varken längd eller gardering pekar rätt” – kompakt, men det är legitim provstrategi riktad till en HP-elev, på svenska, och inte konstruktörsjargong; ordlistans två rader ligger i genrens form. Inga registerbrott, inga tonlägessprång mellan stycken, ingen anglicism – pass på den här dimensionen.

Carrying span: 'Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment in any quarter when at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute, and has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters.' Taken in 23 of 24 => unpaid in exactly 1; 24 quarters = six years, so C is literally true. A dies on the same span: the test is a proportion of sailings inside a ten-minute window, not how far behind the booked minute the average sailing berths. B dies on 'Alison Bexwarden drafted the punctuality clause for the transport authority in 2011' set against 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out' - the clause predates the withdrawal by five years. D dies on 'A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether' plus 'the crossing lost forty-one sailings to weather and a gearbox, and its reliability figure was ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been' - cancellations raise the figure, they do not reduce the payment.

Carrying span: 'He starts with 2005. The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking' - the printed eighteen minutes allowed less than the twenty-four the boat was taking, reinforced by 'the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep, and six of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat.' B dies on Cottam's own 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy' - seventy is now, twenty-five was 2005, and it is not unchanged. C dies for want of any loading claim: the only berthing-work span is 'The linkspan ... was rebuilt in 2013 ... its locking sequence takes a manufacturer's ninety seconds at each berth', which makes that work longer now, not longer then. D dies on 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005' - lateness was being measured in 2005.

Carrying span: Cottam's 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy. Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that,' read against 'the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two' before the certificate ran out. The timetable changes account for 25->32; the lost boat accounts for 32->70, so the withdrawal removed more departures from the day than the timetable changes had. A dies on 'The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out' - padding came first. B dies for want of a span: the only stated reason is 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her'; nothing ties the withdrawal to the linkspan. C dies on 'Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was' - the gap had already stretched 25->32, so the withdrawal was not what first stretched it.

Carrying span: 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes. Where Cattermay's case thins is the join.' Numbers granted, attribution withheld - and 'The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' is the refusal of her cause. A dies on 'Nobody disputes the stamps' - the minutes are conceded, not shown to be little. C dies on 'the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well': the writer withholds the timetable's fault outright, not merely its magnitude. D dies on the same 'Nobody disputes the stamps' (no doubt about the numbers) and again on 'would bear either of the other two just as well' (no grant that the timetable is probably to blame).

Carrying span: the whole spine of the piece - 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005. Last year it was ninety-six' against 'The median time from barrier to far ramp has gone from thirty-nine minutes to fifty-four', with three named parties assigning the gap to different causes ('Something else happened in the middle of my series that I can't take apart yet'; 'the something else is nearly the whole of it'; 'does not accept that it caused any of this'). A dies on 'In the consultation that preceded it, sixty-one per cent of those answering ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go' - passengers were consulted. B dies on 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing' - there is no dispute over which source to believe. C dies on 'None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself' and 'That's the line I'd change ... and nobody writes to me about it' - there is no argument over renewing the clause; the draft carries it 'word for word'.

Backwards method - what each option would require the text to have said. A would require the payment test to be an average-lateness threshold; the text sets a proportion threshold, 'at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute'. Requirement violated. B would require the clause to date from the withdrawal; the text dates it to 2011 twice ('Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment'; 'drafted the punctuality clause ... in 2011') and the withdrawal to 2016. Violated. D would require a partial-reduction mechanic on cancellations; the text supplies the opposite mechanic - 'A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether' - and the worked example of forty-one lost sailings producing 'ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been'. Violated. C would require exactly one missed quarter inside twenty-four; 'has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters' supplies 24-23=1, and twenty-four quarters is six years. Requirement met, so C carries.

Backwards method. B would require Cottam to put 2005 departures seventy minutes apart and unchanged since; his own words put 2005 at twenty-five ('Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes') and seventy at present ('One boat gives you one every seventy'). Violated on both limbs. C would require a stated 2005 loading allowance and loading longer then than now; the text has no loading claim at all, and its nearest span makes berthing work newer and longer ('rebuilt in 2013 ... ninety seconds at each berth'). Unmet. D would require lateness to have gone unmeasured in 2005; 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005' supplies the measurement. Violated. A would require a 2005 booked figure below a 2005 actual figure; 'The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking' supplies exactly that, and 'six of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat' confirms the direction. Met, so A carries.

Backwards method. A would require the 2016 withdrawal to precede the first padding; 'The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out' reverses the order. Violated. B would require some stated linkspan-to-withdrawal link; the only reason given is 'the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her', and the linkspan appears in a separate sentence about axle loads. Unmet. Violated. Met, so D carries.

Backwards method. A would require the writer to discount the fifteen minutes; 'Nobody disputes the stamps' and 'does not contest the fifteen minutes' refuse that. Violated. D would require doubt about her numbers; refused by the same span. Violated. C would require the writer to grant that the timetable is at fault while withholding only the size of the effect; the text withholds the fault itself - 'The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' - so the reading she prefers is one of three live readings, not an established one. Violated. B would require numbers accepted and attribution refused; 'Nobody disputes the stamps' gives the first and 'Where Cattermay's case thins is the join ... she says herself that she cannot pull them apart' gives the second. Backwards method. A would require an unconsulted-passenger strand; the text supplies a consultation with a published result - 'In the consultation that preceded it, sixty-one per cent of those answering ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go'. Violated. B would require a credibility contest between the reliability figure and the stamps; 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing' removes the contest, leaving a dispute about explanation rather than belief. Violated. C would require an argument about carrying the clause into the next contract; 'None of the three is arguing about the sentence Bexwarden raised herself', 'nobody writes to me about it', and a draft that 'carries the 2011 clause word for word' all refuse it. Violated. findings: A: STRONG. Argued at full strength - the option reuses the contract's own vocabulary ('the booked minute'), and the passage is saturated with central-tendency figures (median crossing twenty-four minutes, median barrier-to-ramp thirty-nine to fifty-four), which primes a reader to hear the payment test as an average. Dies on 'at least ninety-two per cent of its sailings berth within ten minutes of the booked minute': the test is the share of sailings inside a fixed window, not the mean lateness. Supported limb = the booked minute and the ten-minute window; refused limb = 'the average sailing'. Teaches the proportion-vs-mean confusion, a real metric misconception.

B: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - the piece puts the clause and the withdrawal in one causal frame (Bexwarden 'does not accept that it caused any of this'), so a reader holding the events but not the dates can fuse them, and the one-boat era is a natural-sounding trigger for writing a punctuality clause. Dies on two dated spans: 'Since 2011 the operator has earned a quality payment' and 'Alison Bexwarden drafted the punctuality clause for the transport authority in 2011' against 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out'. Clause precedes withdrawal by five years. Supported limb = the clause entered the contract at a datable moment; refused limb = that the moment was the withdrawal.

D: STRONGEST on the sheet. Argued at full strength - the passage explicitly connects cancellations to the metric AND flags them as the thing Bexwarden would change, so a reader who registers 'cancellations are handled wrongly here' and then guesses the mechanism will very plausibly guess a partial penalty; 'reduced, though not withdrawn' is exactly the proportionate design a regulator would write, and it is consistent with a naive reading in which a cancelled sailing counts against the ninety-two per cent. Dies twice: 'A sailing that does not run is not late; it leaves the count altogether' inverts the direction, and the worked example settles the sign - 'the crossing lost forty-one sailings to weather and a gearbox, and its reliability figure was ninety-seven per cent, the highest it had ever been'. Supported limb = cancellations do interact with the metric and Bexwarden does object; refused limb = the direction of the interaction.

C (KEY) ARITHMETIC CONFIRMED: 'has taken it in twenty-three of the last twenty-four quarters' gives 24-23 = 1 unpaid quarter, and 24 quarters = 72 months = exactly six years, so 'unpaid in one quarter during the past six years' is precisely true with nothing rounded or approximated.

C (KEY) REWORDING CONFIRMED SOUND: the change from 'one quarter OF the past six years' to 'one quarter DURING the past six years' removes a live ambiguity. 'One quarter of the past six years' admits a fraction reading (a quarter of six years = eighteen months), under which the option would be false; 'during' forces the calendar-quarter reading, under which it is exactly true. The repair fixes a genuine defect rather than churning bytes.
justification: All three distractors pair a text-supported limb with a text-refused limb and each dies on a citable span; none is defensible as a second key. The key's arithmetic reconciles exactly (24 quarters, 23 taken, 1 missed, 72 months = 6 years) and the 'of' to 'during' rewording closes a fraction-reading ambiguity that would otherwise have made the key false on one parse. Pass.

findings: B: MODERATE-STRONG. 'As they still do' borrows plausibility from 'The water is the same width it always was', which primes a nothing-really-changed reading. Dies on the quotation read in order: 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy' assigns seventy to the present, twenty-five to 2005; and 'the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two' refutes 'as they still do'. Supported limb = seventy is a real interval Cottam names; refused limb = its date and the continuity claim.

C: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - the reader has correctly absorbed that the old book under-allowed for something, which is Cottam's actual thesis, and loading is the most available candidate for an under-allowance on a vehicle ferry; the passage even supplies a berthing-procedure duration to lend the idea texture. Dies twice: the passage contains no 2005 loading claim at all, and the direction is inverted by 'The linkspan ... was rebuilt in 2013 for heavier axle loads, and its locking sequence takes a manufacturer's ninety seconds at each berth', which Cottam files under 'work that really has got longer' - longer NOW, not 'longer then than it does now'. Supported limb = the old book under-allowed for something; refused limb = the identity of that something and the direction of change.

D: STRONG. Argued at full strength - genuinely tempting, because Cottam's 'the old seventy-one per cent measured a promise nobody could keep' can be heard as a retrospective judgement rather than a contemporaneous figure, and because the contractual regime demonstrably begins in 2011, six years after the book, which invites the inference that measurement began then too. It also fits the article's arc of a naive old book later disciplined by metrics. Dies on 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005' - a published 2005 figure IS measurement of how late the boat was. Supported limb = the contractual payment regime postdates 2005; refused limb = that measurement as such did.

A (KEY) VERIFIED: 'The median crossing that year took twenty-four minutes against an eighteen-minute booking' plus 'six of the nine added minutes only brought the book level with the boat' - the 2005 book allowed eighteen against an actual twenty-four, uniquely supporting A.
justification: Each distractor is built on a real inference a careful-but-hurried reader makes, and each dies on one span rather than on vagueness. D is the best-constructed of the three because it fails only on a single dated figure while every other element of its reasoning is sound. No distractor is defensible against the key. Pass.

findings: A: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - the chronology is deliberately scattered across paragraphs one, three and five, and a reader anchored on 'In 2005 the crossing ... was printed as eighteen minutes. This year it is printed as twenty-seven' without the intermediate date can read the padding as a recent response to a one-boat service, which is a coherent operational story in its own right. Dies on 'The book went from eighteen minutes to twenty-four in 2013, three years before the certificate ran out' - the interval is spelled out explicitly. Supported limb = both events happened; refused limb = their order.

B: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - the linkspan rebuild and the certificate lapse sit one sentence apart in the same paragraph, and a reader can construct a real-sounding causal bridge: a linkspan 'rebuilt in 2013 for heavier axle loads' is the kind of change that can render an older vessel non-compliant, so the certificate becomes the paperwork symptom of the rebuild. The article's general posture, that official reasons conceal operational ones, encourages exactly this move. Dies for want of any linking span: the text gives one reason and only one - 'in 2016 the relief boat's passenger certificate ran out and the company did not replace her' - and it is a PASSENGER certificate, while the linkspan enters the text for a different purpose (its ninety-second locking sequence as added crossing time). The comparative 'more to do with' demands evidence the text never supplies. Supported limb = both facts exist and are adjacent; refused limb = any causal relation between them.

C: STRONGEST on this item, and the one the stem is really testing. Argued at full strength - Cottam's own words make the boat the whole of the frequency story: 'Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes... One boat gives you one every seventy. Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that.' A reader who takes the named operations director at his word concludes the boat began it. Dies on the writer's deliberate correction in the closing paragraph: 'the interval between departures went from twenty-five minutes to thirty-two' before the certificate lapsed, glossed as 'Some of the frequency was gone before the boat was.' Note the quality of this construction - it dies not on a misreading but on the writer's qualification of a source's overstatement, which is precisely what 'implied' in the stem asks the student to catch. Supported limb = the boat is the dominant frequency cause; refused limb = that it was the first.

D (KEY) VERIFIED, and note the C/D contrast is well engineered: the text supplies the MAGNITUDE (25->32 attributable to the book change, 32->70 once the boat had gone, plus Cottam's 'Pad the book by nothing at all and you'd still have that') while explicitly denying the PRIMACY. D claims magnitude and survives; C claims primacy and dies. The pair is discriminated by the text, not by taste.
justification: Three distractors, three distinct citable kills, and the C/D pair is separated by an explicit textual denial rather than by a judgement call. C is a model distractor: it fails only because the writer corrects the source who states it. Pass.

findings: A: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - the closing paragraph is corrosive in aggregate ('Where Cattermay's case thins is the join'; 'she says herself that she cannot pull them apart'; 'the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well'), so a reader who registers the tone can over-extend the scepticism to the numbers; and A's second clause is exactly right, which lends its first clause borrowed credibility. Dies on 'Nobody disputes the stamps. Cottam has accepted the barrier series in writing, and does not contest the fifteen minutes', reinforced by her unchallenged 'The fifteen minutes are real, and I'd stand behind them in any room.' Supported limb = the explanation is doubted; refused limb = that the minutes are.

C: STRONGEST on the sheet, and the closest thing to a defensible second key anywhere in this unit - examined and rejected. Argued at full strength - C reproduces Cattermay's own hedge almost verbatim in substance ('Ask me how many of them the timetable put there and I'll give you a range, not a number' IS 'at fault, though not by how much'), and the piece's title and opening image, a mate reading a paperback at the slip because the boat is booked to sit there, both point at the timetable. A reader who takes the source's self-description as the writer's verdict lands here honestly. Dies on 'The timetable is the reading she prefers; the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' - that withholds the fault itself, not merely its size: the timetable is one of three readings the same evidence would carry equally, so nothing has been shown. The whole item turns on 'we do not know HOW MUCH' (C) versus 'we do not know WHETHER' (the text), and the text is unambiguous. Not defensible.

D: MODERATE. Argued at full strength - a clean inversion, tempting for a reader who retains that the paragraph contains one concession and one doubt but not which attaches to which; both halves have isolated textual material behind them, since the piece does contain doubt and does present the timetable thesis sympathetically for two paragraphs before correcting it. Dies on both limbs: 'Nobody disputes the stamps' refuses the doubt about numbers, and 'the stamps would bear either of the other two just as well' refuses the grant about the timetable. Weakest of the three because it fails twice, but it is the necessary fourth cell of the 2x2 and it teaches the limb-swap error.

B (KEY) VERIFIED: 'Nobody disputes the stamps' gives acceptance of the numbers, 'Where Cattermay's case thins is the join' gives refusal of the cause. The four options form a complete 2x2 over the two axes, which is why no option is redundant and why the sheet gives no form advantage here.
justification: The 2x2 construction means each distractor teaches a distinct, nameable error - over-extended scepticism (A), fault-established-but-unquantified (C), limb swap (D). C was tested hard as a possible second key and fails on an explicit span; the others fail decisively. Pass.

findings: A (REWRITTEN): well-formed. Supported limb, and unusually strong - 'In 2005 the crossing to the north shore was printed as eighteen minutes. This year it is printed as twenty-seven' (booked slower) with 'The published reliability figure stood at seventy-one per cent in 2005. Last year it was ninety-six' (runs to time more often). That first limb names the article's central paradox correctly, which is what gives the option its pull. Refused limb: 'the passengers who were not consulted' dies on 'In the consultation that preceded it, sixty-one per cent of those answering ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go.' The consultation happened, respondents answered, and their preference is on the record - and it is the load-bearing fact of Bexwarden's defence, 'The clause measures what people asked to have measured.' The option asserts a grievance the text specifically forecloses. One span, decisive.

B (REWRITTEN): well-formed, and pedagogically the best of the three. Supported limb: the two datasets genuinely do tell opposite stories - 'By the only measure the contract knows, the crossing has never run better' against 'The median time from barrier to far ramp has gone from thirty-nine minutes to fifty-four.'
